newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares at one-month low, heading lower.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares at one-month low, heading lower.

text.p: Austrian shares dipped to a one-month low on Tuesday after the ATX index broke through a 200-day moving average and traders said further losses could be in store.
The ATX index of 21 blue-chip shares fell 14.35 points, or 1.33 percent, to 1,062.24 points. Two issues ended in positive territory and 19 were down.
"Technically the market looks as if it will go lower," said a trader, noting that a 200-day moving average at 1,067-1,068 had failed to brake the ATX's slide.
He forecast a test of support at 1,050 points on Wednesday. Others predicted the market would manage to hold above 1,060.
"Admittedly support has given but I still see the market in an upward trend," said a trader at another bank.
Semi-conductor maker Austria Mikro Systeme (AMS) was the biggest decliner, continuing a slide ahead of nine-month earnings data due on Thursday.
AMS finished 38 schillings, or 4.89 percent down, at 748.50 schillings. The firm posted a group pre-tax loss of 3.1 million schillings in the first half.
Traders said a decline in the share price of telecoms firms Ericsson and Nokia may also have contributed to AMS weakness.
Bank Austria was the biggest gainer, climbing three schillings, or 0.72 percent, to 419 schillings.
November ATX futures stood 16.0 points down at 1,064. The broad-based Vienna bourse index shed 4.14 points, or one percent, to end at 408.19 points. -- Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
